The review of the [[Meclib Workbench]] (Questions page, **Review** at the top of the editor) checks a question against the conventions for STACK questions with meclib whenever it is opened or saved. Each finding has a key `rule[target]`, a level, a message and, where possible, an automatic fix with a preview of the changed XML.

**Levels**
- **required**: Moodle refuses the question, or it does not work as intended
- **recommended**: meclib conventions (style guide, wiki pages of the feedback functions)
- **hint**: worth a look; a fix, if offered, is not preselected

"Apply selected, reject the rest" records the unchecked proposals as rejected in the question description (internal field): `Review rejected: <rule[target]>, ...`. Rejected findings are shown greyed and do not count as open.

## Security

### `security`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_security()`

Identifiers STACK refuses in a question (its security list: functions like system(), eval_string(), concat() of names ...): STACK does not save such a question. Checked: the model answers and texts (as the preview's check), the question variables and the feedback variables of the PRTs, statement by statement. Rename or replace the identifier.

Messages:
> question variables, line …: …
> PRT …, feedback variables, line …: …

## Texts and layout

### `layout.style-typo`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_style_typo()`

A doubled style attribute style=style="..." in the question text or the general/specific feedback (a slip of older templates): browsers ignore the style, so e.g. the graphic no longer floats beside the text. The fix removes the duplicate.

Message:
> …: style=style="..." - browsers ignore this style (the graphic no longer floats). Remove the duplicate style=.

### `layout.float-margin`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_float_margin()`

A block floating right or left (usually the graphic, `<div style="float:right">`) without a margin: the text runs into it. The fix adds the margin of the workbench template (right: 0 0 0.5em 1.5em, left: 0 1.5em 0.5em 0). One finding per text; after the fix a new review finds the next block.

Message:
> …: the …-aligned block (graphic) has no margin, the text runs into it. Add margin: … (as in the workbench template).

### `lang.declaration`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_lang()`

A question that uses meclib feedback functions (an fb_*.mac include) but declares no languages in the question text: STACK then shows the English texts of the feedback functions. The fix inserts the empty declaration `[[lang code="de"]]` `[[/lang]]``[[lang code="other"]]` `[[/lang]]` after the graphic (wiki "Multilingual questions").

Message:
> The question uses meclib feedback functions but declares no languages; STACK then shows their English texts. Insert the empty declaration … (after the graphic).

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Multilingual-questions

### `text.math-delimiters`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_math_delimiters()`

Math delimiters by the format of each text: in HTML texts `\( ... \)`; in Markdown texts the strict form `\\\( ... \\\)` (backslash and bracket both escaped, so Markdown never takes the bracket for part of a link), except inside block-level HTML (a line starting with `<p>`, `<table>`, `<div>` ... up to its closing tag), which Markdown passes through unchanged: there `\( ... \)` as in HTML. Checked: question text, general and specific feedback, question note, PRT node feedback, each by its own format; only complete pairs, not in `[[jsxgraph]]` blocks or `{@...@}`/`{#...#}`. The fix rewrites the delimiters.

### `text.raw-in-math`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_raw_in_math()`

`{#...#}` inside a formula: Moodle shows the castext unevaluated in some places (question bank, import), MathJax then fails on "#" ("macro parameter character"), and Moodle refuses to save it; `{@...@}` gives the LaTeX of the value, without delimiters inside a formula.

Message:
> …: …× `{#...#}` inside `\(` `\)` or `\[` `\]` → `{@...@}`. Unevaluated (question bank, import), MathJax fails on "#" and Moodle does not save the question; `{@...@}` gives the LaTeX of the value and adds no delimiters inside a formula.

## Inputs

### `inputs.graphic`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_graphic_inputs()`

The hidden inputs bound to a meclib graphic (`[[jsxgraph input-ref-...]]`).

The input of the objects (stateRef) is a string input, the input of the names (fbd_names) an algebraic input with floats allowed; neither shows validation or asks students to verify (wiki "MecLib Question Setup"). The fix sets these options.

Message:
> Input … (bound to the graphic as …): ….

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/MecLib-Question-Setup

### `inputs.graphic-visible`

Level: **hint** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_graphic_inputs()`

The hidden inputs bound to a meclib graphic (`[[jsxgraph input-ref-...]]`).

An input of the graphic that is not inside `<p hidden> ... </p>`: students see the raw data (fine while debugging).

Message:
> `[[input:…]]` is not inside `<p hidden> ... </p>`: students see the raw data (fine while debugging).

### `inputs.settings`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_input_settings()`

The answer inputs (algebraic, units, numerical; not the inputs of a graphic).

As the style guide and the maintainer decided - insert stars for spaces only (none for numerical inputs), the syntax hint as placeholder, validation "compact", students must verify. The fix sets these options.

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Style-Guide-for-Questions-in-Engineering-Mechanics

### `inputs.syntaxhint`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_input_settings()`

The answer inputs (algebraic, units, numerical; not the inputs of a graphic).

Syntax hints that are empty or plain words ("expression", "Zahl", ...) become the multilingual hints of fb_value.mac (`{@meclib_h_alg@}`, `{@meclib_h_number@}`, `{@meclib_h_unit@}`); the fix adds the include of fb_value.mac if the question lacks it.

Messages:
> Input …: syntax hint … → … (German/English, from fb_value.mac).
> Input …: syntax hint … → … (German/English); this adds stack_include("…") to the question variables.

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Multilingual-questions

### `feedback.inputs`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_feedback_inputs()`

Input names in the CAS parts of the specific or general feedback: STACK evaluates these texts once when the question starts, with the question variables only, so an input there is just an unbound symbol. The answers reach the specific feedback through `[[feedback:..]]` of a PRT whose feedback shows what depends on them.

Message:
> …: …. STACK evaluates the CAS parts of the … when the question starts, without the answers, so the input is an unbound symbol there. Move this part into the feedback of a PRT (e.g. a formative PRT, feedback style 0) and place its `[[feedback:..]]` in the specific feedback.

### `matrix.feedback`

Level: **recommended / hint** · automatic fix: **partly** · function `r_matrix_inputs()`

Matrix inputs (wiki "Matrix input", "Matrix Feedback").

Element-wise feedback. PRT X gets the feedback variable [txt, isOK]: fb_unit_matrix(S_X, T, tol) (numeric: a numeric answer test, fb_unit or the old toList pattern; the answer test becomes AlgEquiv isOK = true, toList is removed) or txt: fb_vars_matrix(S_X, T, vars) (otherwise; AlgEquiv on the matrix stays), feedback `{@txt@}` in both branches, quiet. T is the input's model answer; tolerance and vars are taken from the old PRT, simple symbol labels of the old per-component feedback become the label list. PRTs with several nodes or other feedback text get a hint only.

Messages:
> PRT … (matrix input …): add  …  to the feedback variables; feedback `{@txt@}` in both branches, quiet…. Labels: ….
> PRT … (matrix input …): convert it to … by hand, ….

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Matrix-Feedback

### `matrix.layout`

Level: **recommended / hint** · automatic fix: **partly** · function `r_matrix_inputs()`

Matrix inputs (wiki "Matrix input", "Matrix Feedback").

STACK shows a matrix input as a block of its own, so label, matrix and validation do not stand side by side in a paragraph. A paragraph `<p>`label `[[input:S_X]]` `[[validation:S_X]]` `[[feedback:X]]``</p>` becomes a table row label | input | validation with the feedback below; other layouts get a hint only.

Messages:
> Input … (matrix): STACK shows a matrix input as a block of its own, so the label, the matrix and the validation do not stand side by side in a paragraph. Put them into a table row, the feedback below it.
> Input … (matrix) is not in a table row label | input | validation; this layout is not converted automatically.

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Matrix-input

## PRTs and grading

### `prt.simp`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_prts()`

Settings of the PRTs:

A PRT that uses fb_unit() should have simplification off, so that answers like 0*kg keep their unit for the feedback.

Message:
> PRT … uses fb_unit: switch simplification off, so that answers like 0*kg keep their unit for the feedback….

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/fb_unit

### `prt.feedbackformat`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_prts()`

Settings of the PRTs:

Every branch of every PRT in format html. Markdown is only the default of question generators; in Moodle it suppresses the yellow feedback background (the workbench preview shows it anyway), and STACK escapes texts inserted with `{@...@}`, e.g. the `[[lang]]` blocks of meclib feedback. STACK wants one format per PRT, so the fix sets all branches.

Message:
> PRT …: feedback format … → html for all nodes. In Markdown, Moodle shows the feedback without the yellow background, and STACK escapes texts inserted with `{@...@}` (e.g. `[[lang]]` blocks of meclib feedback)….

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Meclib-tutorial:-Add-Meclib-feedback-functions

### `prt.feedbackstyle`

Level: **recommended / hint** · automatic fix: **partly** · function `r_prts()`

Settings of the PRTs:

Feedback style compact (2); a hint only where the feedback contains HTML blocks (`<p>`, `<div>`, lists), which need the standard style.

Messages:
> PRT …: feedback style is not compact, but its feedback contains HTML blocks (`<p>`, `<div>`, lists), which need the standard style.
> PRT …: feedback style … → compact (2).

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Style-Guide-for-Questions-in-Engineering-Mechanics

### `prt.quiet`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_prts()`

Settings of the PRTs:

Where the feedback comes from a meclib function, the answer test's own feedback is switched off (quiet).

Message:
> PRT …: the feedback comes from a meclib function; switch the answer test's own feedback off (quiet).

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Meclib-tutorial:-Add-Meclib-feedback-functions

### `prt.tolerance`

Level: **hint** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_prts()`

Settings of the PRTs:

A relative tolerance other than 0.005 (the maintainer's standard) is a hint.

Message:
> PRT …: … with tolerance …; standard is ….

### `grade.default`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_grade()`

A question with PRTs but default mark 0 gives no points. The fix sets the default mark to 1.

Message:
> The question has PRTs but default mark 0: it gives no points. Set it to 1.

### `prt.fb-floats`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_fb_floats()`

meclib feedback on the answers to algebraic and numerical inputs.

(1) `{@fb_vars(sans, tans, ...)@}` in the feedback of a PRT node becomes [txt, ok]: fb_floats(sans, tans, 0.005); in the PRT's feedback variables and `{@txt@}` in the feedback; the list of variables (3rd argument) and the tolerance (5th) of fb_vars are dropped, fb_floats marks the deviating terms itself. (2) A node with AlgEquiv that compares an algebraic input with its model answer and has no meclib feedback gets the same, `{@txt@}` at the start of its false branch (also if the false branch goes on to nodes for typical errors: the feedback of fb_floats is generic). (3) A node that compares a numerical input with its model answer gets `{@fb_unit(sans, tans, tol)@}` at the start of its false branch (tol: the tolerance of NumRelative, else 0.005). Names txt1, ok1, ... for several calls in one PRT or where txt/ok are taken. All nodes of the PRT get the format html (one format per PRT; in Markdown, STACK escapes the inserted text, e.g. the `[[lang]]` blocks). The nodes become quiet; the answer tests stay (ok is not used, the grading does not change). If fb_floats comes in and the question variables lack fb_dims, the fix adds fb_dims: []; to fill in (see qv.fb-dims).

Message:
> PRT …: …. fb_floats(sans, tans, 0.005) goes into the feedback variables as [txt, ok], `{@txt@}` into the feedback (at the start of the false branch); fb_unit() directly into the false branch; the nodes become quiet; the answer tests stay (the grading does not change).…

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/fb_floats()

### `prt.fb-vars-label`

Level: **hint** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_fb_floats()`

meclib feedback on the answers to algebraic and numerical inputs.

Calls of fb_vars with a label (4th argument, e.g. for vector components): fb_vars shows the label only when it has something to say, fb_floats has none; no automatic fix.

Message:
> …: fb_vars() with a label (…); fb_floats() has none, convert by hand (e.g. vector components).

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/fb_floats()

## Maxima code and includes

### `include.lang-specific`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_lang_includes()`

Includes of the obsolete language-specific libraries fb_*_EN.mac / fb_*_DE.mac: the feedback functions are multilingual. The fix includes fb_*.mac instead.

Message:
> …_….mac is obsolete since the feedback functions are multilingual; include ….mac.

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Multilingual-questions

### `maxima.multsgn`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_multsgn()`

make_multsgn() with an option STACK does not know: STACK refuses the question ("make_multsgn received un-supported option"). "blank" was an option until STACK 2025033100 (a thin space); the fix replaces it by "onum" (a cross between numbers only, no space between numbers), everywhere in the question. Other options are reported without a fix.

Message:
> …× make_multsgn("…"): STACK knows only … and refuses the question ("make_multsgn received un-supported option").…

### `qv.fb-dims`

Level: **hint** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_fb_dims()`

The question uses fb_floats() without the units of the variables (fb_dims missing or empty), so its unit check is off. Declare fb_dims: [a = "m", q_0 = "N/m", ...] in the question variables (wiki fb_floats(), Units).

Message:
> The question uses fb_floats(), but fb_dims …: without the units of the variables there is no unit check. Declare e.g. fb_dims: [a = "m", q_0 = "N/m"]; in the question variables.

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/fb_floats()#units

### `qv.unit-name`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_unit_names()`

A question variable named like a STACK unit (g, m, mm, s, N, t, h, ...) in a question in units mode: the value hides the unit inside the question, and in a student's answer the name counts as the unit (STACK allows unit names before it forbids the teacher's variable names) - e.g. "m g" of a meclib force in the names input only works because g is also gram. Without units mode the same answer would be invalid. Rename the variable (g -> g0).

Message:
> The question is in units mode, where … is a STACK unit. The question variable … hides the unit in the question, and in answers … still counts as the unit: e.g. a meclib force "m g" in the names input is accepted only because … is also a unit - in a question without units it would be rejected as a question variable. In grading the unit is replaced by the variable's value: an answer using the unit … is accepted as valid and marked wrong (STACK 4.13.1: 300000 g m/s^2 for 300 N with g: 10*m/s^2 gives ATUnits_incompatible_units). Rename the variable (e.g. …0).

### `maxima.semicolon`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_semicolons()`

Missing statement separators in Maxima code: STACK's parser assumes a ; where a line ends a complete statement and the next line starts an assignment or call (the preview reports these as "missing ; assumed"); the fix writes the ; into the file.

Messages:
> Question variables: no ; at the end of the statement in line … (STACK assumes one). Add it.
> PRT …, feedback variables: no ; at the end of the statement in line … (STACK assumes one). Add it.

### `include.branch`

Level: **hint** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_include_branch()`

Includes of meclib from a branch other than main (e.g. the dev branch while a feature is not merged yet): a reminder to switch back after the merge; the fix only after it, as main may not have the functions yet.

Message:
> … is included from the branch …, not from main. Switch to main once … is merged into main (before that, main may lack functions the question uses).

### `include.dist`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_include_dist()`

Includes of the compact copies in Maxima/dist/ (removed 2026-10-23: STACK drops comments when it reads the code, so they did not make its compilation faster): STACK refuses the question as soon as it compiles it again ("could not retrieve").

Message:
> … is included from Maxima/dist/, which no longer exists (the compact copies did not make STACK faster). STACK refuses the question as soon as it compiles it again ("could not retrieve"). Include Maxima/… instead.

### `include.unused`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_includes()`

Includes of meclib's Maxima files.

An included file of which the question uses no function and no variable; the fix removes its stack_include (loading it only costs compile time, which shows as CAS timeouts in Moodle).

Uses are searched in all Maxima code: question variables, feedback variables, CAS parts of the texts and of the syntax hints, model answers, PRT nodes (SAns, TAns, test options); a function counts only when called ("angle("), so that a variable of the same name does not count. Files needed by a needed file count as needed; *_EN.mac files are never proposed.

What other findings of the review will need counts as used, so that their fixes and this one do not contradict: a local copy of a function of an included file (functions.legacy deletes it), and the syntax hints `{@meclib_h_...@}` that inputs.syntaxhint puts in (fb_value.mac).

Message:
> … is included, but the question uses none of its functions or variables. Loading it costs compile time (CAS timeouts in Moodle). The fix removes the stack_include.

### `include.missing`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_includes()`

Includes of meclib's Maxima files.

A meclib function or variable used without its file (it would stay unevaluated); the fix adds the include, from the same branch as the question's other meclib includes.

Uses are searched in all Maxima code: question variables, feedback variables, CAS parts of the texts and of the syntax hints, model answers, PRT nodes (SAns, TAns, test options); a function counts only when called ("angle("), so that a variable of the same name does not count. Files needed by a needed file count as needed; *_EN.mac files are never proposed.

What other findings of the review will need counts as used, so that their fixes and this one do not contradict: a local copy of a function of an included file (functions.legacy deletes it), and the syntax hints `{@meclib_h_...@}` that inputs.syntaxhint puts in (fb_value.mac).

Message:
> … is used, but … is not included; without it the call stays unevaluated. The fix adds stack_include("…").

### `functions.legacy`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_legacy_functions()`

Old copies of meclib functions in the question variables (from the time before stack_include): the include provides the current version; the local definition hides it or duplicates it. Reported when a meclib Maxima file defines the function too and that file is included, or the name starts with fb_. The fix deletes the definition and adds the include if missing.

Message:
> The question variables define …(), which meclib's … provides…. The local copy is probably an old version and hides the current one. Delete it….

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/Home

## Graphics (meclib)

### `state.locked`

Level: **recommended / hint** · automatic fix: **partly** · function `r_locked()`

The legacy object state "locked" in the objects of a meclib graphic (initdata etc.): fb_system() counts only "SHOW"/"show" as shown. Replacing it by "SHOW" is offered (recommended, with fix) for the object types with a regression test for this - types that appear with "SHOW" in a scene of tests/scenes/ (state_show.json: beam, q, fix1, fix12, fix123, bar, force, moment); other types get a hint only. Not reported: types for which "locked" is a state of their own (spline: active, inactive, locked, pure; no "SHOW").

Messages:
> Objects of type … with the legacy state "locked": replace by "SHOW" (fb_system() counts only "SHOW" as shown; regression test: tests/scenes/state_show.json).
> State "locked" in objects of type …. Replacing it by "SHOW" is offered only for types with a regression test for this (a scene in tests/scenes/ with the type in state "SHOW").

### `graphic.missing-input`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_scenes()`

`[[jsxgraph]]` blocks and the inputs they are bound to (input-ref-...): graphics in the feedback must be static, a bound input must exist, a hidden (or missing) input of a former interactive graphic is left over.

Message:
> Question text, graphic …: input-ref-… refers to …, which the question does not have; Moodle then does not save the question. Remove the binding….

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/MecLib-Question-Setup

### `graphic.unused-input`

Level: **hint** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_scenes()`

`[[jsxgraph]]` blocks and the inputs they are bound to (input-ref-...): graphics in the feedback must be static, a bound input must exist, a hidden (or missing) input of a former interactive graphic is left over.

Message:
> Input … is …, no graphic is bound to it and no PRT uses it (left over from an interactive graphic?). Delete it….

### `graphic.feedback-interactive`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_scenes()`

`[[jsxgraph]]` blocks and the inputs they are bound to (input-ref-...): graphics in the feedback must be static, a bound input must exist, a hidden (or missing) input of a former interactive graphic is left over.

Message:
> …, graphic …: it is bound to …, but a graphic in the feedback has no inputs. Make it static (no input-ref attributes, var stateRef; in the header).

See also: https://github.com/mkraska/meclib/wiki/MecLib-Question-Setup

### `index.literal`

Level: **hint** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_literal_index()`

Object indices written as numbers in calls of meclib feedback functions (fb_fix12(obj, n, 7, ...)): the numbers change when objects are inserted into the graphic. Define a variable for each object index (i_A: 7; /* fix12 A */) and use it.

Message:
> …: …. Define a variable for each object index (e.g. i_A: 7; /* fix12 A */) and use it here; the numbers change when objects are inserted.

### `tans.copy`

Level: **hint** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_tans_copy()`

The model answer of a graphic's input is its initial state (tans equal to init): usually it is derived from it, tansdata: copy(initdata) with the changes a student makes, tans: stackjson_stringify(tansdata).

Message:
> The model answer of … is the initial state (init). Usually it is derived from it: tansdata: copy(initdata) with changes, tans: stackjson_stringify(tansdata).

## Files, variants and question tests

### `variants.none`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_variants()`

Randomised questions (STACK's rule: a word of the question variables beginning with rand, multiselqn or stack_seed; agents/stack_essentials.md, "Deploy variants").

No deployed variant. Students may get any variant, including one nobody has tested, and the API runs no tests. Deploy variants in the Tests column (survey of seeds).

Message:
> The question is randomised but has no deployed variants: students may get any variant, also one nobody has tested, and STACK runs no tests. Deploy variants in the Tests column (survey of seeds, distinct question notes).

### `variants.note`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_variants()`

Randomised questions (STACK's rule: a word of the question variables beginning with rand, multiselqn or stack_seed; agents/stack_essentials.md, "Deploy variants").

The question note is empty. STACK tells variants apart by their notes only; show every value that distinguishes the variants, and the answer.

Message:
> The question note is empty: STACK tells variants apart by their notes only. Show every value that distinguishes the variants, and the answer, e.g. `\(`F = `{@F@}``\)`, answer `{@ta1@}`.

### `variants.rand-name`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **no** · function `r_variants()`

Randomised questions (STACK's rule: a word of the question variables beginning with rand, multiselqn or stack_seed; agents/stack_essentials.md, "Deploy variants").

A question variable whose name begins with rand makes STACK treat the question as randomised; rename it.

Message:
> The question variable … begins with "rand": STACK then treats the question as randomised (deployed variants, tests per variant). Rename it.

### `files.unused`

Level: **recommended** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_unused_files()`

Files embedded in the question (`<file>` elements of its texts) that no text references as `@@PLUGINFILE@@/name` - typically leftovers of earlier versions edited in Moodle. Shown with the image; the fix removes them (all `<file>` elements of that name in the question).

Message:
> … (… kB…) is stored in …, but no text shows it - left over from an earlier version (e.g. an image replaced in Moodle's editor, which keeps the old file).… Remove it.

### `tests.value-length`

Level: **required** · automatic fix: **yes** · function `r_qtest_length()`

Test input values longer than STACK's database column (255 characters): the import into Moodle fails with "error writing to the database". The fix moves them into question variables.

Message:
> Test …: the value of … is longer than the 255 characters STACK can store for a test input; importing the question into Moodle fails ("error writing to the database"). The fix moves it into a question variable (…), the test input then holds its name.
